fields.v: Success criterion: none stated by the authors. Metrics: accuracy conditional on valid submission (bootstrap 95% CIs; most absolute values only in Figs. 2-3) and, on ProgramBench, constraint erosion per compaction (Table 3). Scaffold OpenCode for all (version not stated). Threshold sweep 160K-380K (self-summarization baseline): - Claude Opus 4.6 (max effort): accuracy similar across thresholds on all benchmarks; erosion 0.51 of 3 rule categories per compaction, >=1 dropped 43%, never all 3. - GPT-5.4 (medium): accuracy similar across thresholds (PaperBench 0.59 at 160K baseline); erosion 1.76 of 3 (>=1 90%, all 3 25%). - GPT-5.3-Codex (medium, 400K window): PaperBench 0.38 at 160K -> about 0.60 at >=260K; ProgramBench generally flat; PostTrainBench inconclusive (wide overlapping CIs); erosion 2.73 of 3 (>=1 99%, all 3 80%). - Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (high): rarely compacts (1.00 compactions per run at 160K); uninformative; ProgramBench results excluded (reward hacking); not run on PostTrainBench. Strategies at 160K (no strategy better than baseline beyond CIs on any benchmark; ProgramBench: no strategy significantly changes performance): - Tool-output pruning: close to baseline for all models on PaperBench. - Filesystem offloading: near baseline on PaperBench for the 1M models; GPT-5.3-Codex 0.38 -> about 0.24. - Clear thinking: GPT-5.4 PaperBench 0.59 -> 0.43; no drop for Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.3-Codex. - Small-model summary (Haiku 4.5): Opus 4.6 within baseline CI; GPT-5.4 0.59 -> 0.43; GPT-5.3-Codex 0.38 -> 0.18. Erosion not measured per strategy; no cost metric. Quality and cost verdict for every configuration above: no criterion stated by the authors

fields.v: Benchmarks: PaperBench (3 papers), ProgramBench (2 tasks), PostTrainBench (2 base models x 3 targets). Configurations: 5 compaction strategies at 160K threshold; thresholds 160K/180K/200K/260K/320K/380K for baseline; 4 models. Baseline: self-summarization by the same model. Held constant: scaffold (OpenCode), trigger mechanism, summarization prompt, benchmark settings (time limits, hardware). Acceptance: benchmark graders (rubric LLM judge, tests, target benchmark). Repetitions: 2 runs per task and configuration; runs relaunched until enough succeeded (attempts vary). Human intervention: none. Gemini not run on PostTrainBench; ProgramBench Gemini results excluded (reward hacking)

fields.v: Threshold does not affect 1M-context models; GPT-5.3-Codex worse at low thresholds on PaperBench (0.38 vs ~0.60). No strategy beats self-summarization; discarding strategies cost some models up to 20 points on PaperBench (e.g. GPT-5.4 0.59 -> 0.43) and leave others unaffected. Constraint erosion: ~0.92 rule categories dropped at first compaction, 1.93 by 10th, 2.41 by 15th, 2.65 by 30th. SWE-chat: 81% of constraints preserved, 19% dropped (24.5% with second judge); feature requirements dropped 6.2%, process instructions 35.9%, scope exclusions 36.8%. Significance via overlapping bootstrap CIs only, no formal tests

fields.v: Distinguished models on threshold and some strategies on PaperBench; PostTrainBench error bars too wide to conclude; Gemini uninformative. Repeatability: 2 runs per configuration, bootstrap CIs; code released. Limitations stated: four models, three benchmarks, few tasks per benchmark (cost and compute); one scaffold; Gemini rarely compacts and reward hacks; SWE-chat sessions from a different scaffold (Claude Code) and models; Q4 measures loss but not its effect on outcomes; threshold range covers only 16-38% of 1M windows

fields.v: Current benchmarks are compaction-friendly (fixed objective, progress on disk), so they hide constraint loss; constraints on how to work and what not to do are dropped first, even when the prompt asks to keep them. Future: compare subagent decomposition with compaction under the same scaffold; harder evaluations with constraints not recoverable from the filesystem (multi-turn sessions with changing user instructions)
